fatal_errors: The proposed coating intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.

It incorrectly treats W–Cu interdiffusion as the central cause of phase separation and voiding, although W and Cu are strongly immiscible; the target mechanism instead relies on selective Ti extraction and formation of a spontaneous W-rich passivating interlayer.
An added TiN or W2C layer may increase interfacial thermal resistance or impair Cu infiltration and wetting, so improved thermal conductivity cannot be inferred merely from reduced interdiffusion.
The service claim invokes moderate-to-high neutron flux, but neither the cited evidence nor the proposed ion-beam experiment establishes neutron-irradiation performance.
explanation: The hypothesis is thematically aligned with W/Cu joining, interface stability, heat transfer, and irradiation, and it provides a reasonably controlled coated-versus-uncoated falsification test. However, it misses the target precursor, selective liquid-metal-dealloying intervention, bicontinuous RHEA/Cu architecture, W-rich interlayer, quantitative processing conditions, and measured thermal and helium-implantation outcomes. Its mechanism is also weak because W and Cu have limited mutual solubility, while a refractory coating can itself reduce thermal transport. E1 supports only the general fusion-joint context and need for an interlayer; E2 concerns coated diamond in an HEA and does not validate TiN or W2C barriers in W–Cu. Thus, the proposal is testable but not adequately supported and is not a reconstruction of the target study.
